d: What Papertooth is, what it gives a page, and how the CSS and the optional script divide the work between them.
x: Hand-drawn stationery for the web. Paper-makers call the fine grain on a sheet its tooth: it is what grips the pencil and what you feel under your fingers. Papertooth brings that feel to a web page, inspired by Japanese stationery. Writing that looks like it was done by hand, on paper you can almost feel. Text sits on the dots. Links get a pen underline, a phrase can be picked out with a highlighter, and a word can be circled in red pencil. Get startedBrowse the kit Every element has a playground 済 Approved What is inside Paper and writing Paper, ruling, typed and handwritten textMarks Highlighters, underlines, separators, marks, stampsPaper goods Sticky notes, tape, cards, clips, labelsImages Lithograph, printer, framesPlanner Day, week, habits, bullet journalForms Checkboxes, radios, text fieldsDiagrams Flowcharts, pie and bar charts from Mermaid How it works The CSS works on its own: paper, tape, notes, stamps, forms and every variant are classes and data attributes. A small optional script adds what CSS cannot do: ink textures as SVG filters, shapes drawn at each element's real size, text snapped to the grid, image effects and diagrams. It draws only what is near the screen and goes fully idle afterwards. Nothing is rotated unless you ask for it. Give any note, stamp, tape, card or photo a --pt-rot to set it at an angle. Anything drawn can be drawn with any instrument: fountain pen, ballpoint, brush pen, felt marker, graphite or coloured pencil. Put data-tool on it.

d: Install Papertooth from npm or load the stylesheet and script from a CDN, with the one line of markup a page needs.
x: papertooth · Getting started Install the package, or load two files from a CDN. npm npm install papertooth import 'papertooth/css'; import { init } from 'papertooth'; const kit = init({ pen: 'ink-ai', motion: 'scroll' }); CDN, no build step <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/papertooth@0.5/dist/papertooth.min.css" <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/papertooth@0.5/dist/papertooth.min.js" defer data-pt-auto</script data-pt-auto starts the script on load. Pass options as JSON: data-pt-auto='{"seed": 7}'. The running instance is window.Papertooth.kit. Fonts Fonts are not bundled. The defaults are Courier Prime, Special Elite and Caveat, plus Shippori Mincho B1 and Zen Maru Gothic for Japanese stamps. Swap any of them in Theming. <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Caveat:wght@400;700&family=Courier+Prime:wght@400;700&family=Special+Elite&display=swap" A first page <body class="pt-desk" <main class="pt-sheet" data-paper="dot" <h1 class="pt-wobble"A typed heading</h1 <pSome text with a <mark class="pt-mark"highlight</mark and a <a class="pt-link" href=""link</a.</p <a class="pt-btn" href=""Hire me</a </main </body Without the script Everything still renders, with a fixed version of each drawn shape. For the textures, paste dist/papertooth-filters.svg into the page and add class="pt-filters" to <html. Lithograph, printer and diagrams need the script.

d: Every option init() takes and every method on the kit it returns, with what each one is for.
x: papertooth · Reference Options for init(), and the methods on the returned kit. const kit = Papertooth.init({ root: document.body, // where to look seed: null, // a number makes every drawing repeatable filters: true, // inject the texture filters filterParams: { // tune any texture text: { density: .7 }, head: { rough: 1, density: .8 }, graphite: { tooth: 2.4, rough: .9 }, stamp: { wear: .55, rough: 1.3, edge: .5, mottle: .5 }, smudge: { drag: 4.2, blur: 3.4, strength: .78 }, smear: { drag: 7, blur: 4.5, strength: .7 }, typewriter: { spread: .6, rough: 1.2, uneven: .7, speckle: .5 } }, snap: true, // put text on the grid lazy: true, // draw shapes only near the screen motion: 'scroll', // 'scroll', 'load' or 'none' stagger: .12, // seconds between marks drawing on in one block highlight: 'swipe', // default highlighter outline: 'sketch', // default outline observe: true, // enhance elements added later today: true, // fill planner pieces marked data-today pen: null, pencil: null, ribbon: null, highlighter: null }); kit.setPen('ink-beni'); // a token name or any colour kit.setPencil('pencil-2b'); kit.setRibbon('ribbon-blue'); kit.setHighlighter('ffc06a'); kit.setFilters({ stamp: { wear: .8 } }); kit.setTypewriter({ spread: .8 }); kit.refresh(); // after changing writing mode or layout kit.replay(); // draw everything on again kit.destroy(); Papertooth.renderDiagram(source, { font, seed, fill }); // SVG string Papertooth.filtersMarkup(params); // the filters as SVG markup Performance - Shapes are drawn only when they come near the screen, and redrawn only when their size or style changes. - Each frame measures everything first and writes everything after, so the page lays out once. - Snapping uses translate, which moves text without a new layout. - The script ignores its own changes to the page and goes idle after loading. - Animations are CSS only and stop for people who prefer reduced motion. - Textures are SVG filters on text only. On long pages, use .pt-texture-light, or .pt-lazy on sections so the browser can skip them off screen.

d: Every released version of papertooth, newest first, with what changed in each — and an Atom feed to follow new ones.
x: papertooth · Releases Newest first. Follow by feed. 0.5.2 - 2026-10-29 29 October 2026 Fixed - A node id with a hyphen broke a flowchart. my-node -- other was read as a node called my, and the edge after it was dropped without a word, leaving a stray node and no line. Ids keep their hyphens, and the Mermaid subset now has its own tests. - A date stamp filled again in another language kept the lang="ja" it was given the first time, so a screen reader went on announcing the new text as Japanese. - An annotation whose ink <svg was written by hand with whitespace inside it threw while drawing, because the whitespace counted as one of its paths. - A diagram or an image effect that finished loading after destroy() could still schedule a paint into a kit that was gone. 0.5.1 - 2026-10-29 29 October 2026 Fixed - Three-digit hex colours threw instead of resolving. toRgb read the colour with Arrayslice, which a string does not have, so abc failed wherever a colour is given as a short hex: setPen, setPencil, setRibbon and setHighlighter, the matching init() options (and the same keys in data-pt-auto), the ink filters, and the lithograph's ink. Six-digit hex, rgb() and the pt- token names were never affected. 0.5.0 - 2026-10-24 24 October 2026 Added - Your own content in date stamp cells: a stamp picture, a letter, a mark, anything. Put an element inside the stamp with data-day, data-date or data-month (and data-row for a row to fill in); in React, return it from cell({ part, row, date, state }). It sits with the pencil marks, on top of the printed stamp, and stays when the stamp is filled again. - Row labels: data-rows="Run, Read, Water" (or rows={['Run', 'Read', 'Water']}) writes them in a first column, on the wide month and the week strip. - Every cell from stampCells() and stampLayout() carries the date it stands for, and cells in rows to fill in carry their row. - A day heading and a week can show any day with data-date="2026-10-21" (until now only today, with data-today), and are written in data-locale or the page's lang. - data-week-label="Semaine {n}" words a day heading's week number in any language (weekLabel in React also takes this string). - data-mark on a week (mark on <Week): today circled, boxed, highlighted or left plain. - cell({ habit, day, done }) on <Habits draws a cell yourself, in place of its checkbox: a stamp, a letter, anything. - The README shows how to use your own picture as a stamp (--pt-pic). Fixed - A day heading always wrote "Week" in English, and the script filled day headings and weeks in British English whatever the page's language. - A week's circle on today replaced the date's own style attribute, and filling the week again for another date left the old mark's settings behind. The circle's colour and offsets now come from the stylesheet. 0.4.1 - 2026-10-23 23 October 2026 Changed - The brush looks like brush ink: a heavier stroke with a ragged edge, dry streaks where the brush runs out, and uneven ink, on marks, checkboxes, diagrams, and drawn underlines and rules. Before, it was a thick, even line, close to the fountain pen and the marker. Tune it with setFilters({ brush: { dry, rough } }). - A date stamp tells screen readers what it marks: a month calendar says the day it marks (Wednesday 21 October 2026), a year of months says the month.
